outcome: NICU admission rate for respiratory insufficiency
cohort: The study included 395 women who underwent non-elective cesarean sections between 2021 and 2023.
finding: General anesthesia in non-elective cesarean sections is associated with worse neonatal outcomes, extending beyond the resuscitation phase to sustained NICU morbidity.
mod_finding: General anesthesia during non-elective cesarean sections is associated with increased odds of neonatal resuscitation, NICU admission, lower Apgar scores at 1 minute, and higher rates of respiratory support in the NICU compared to neuraxial anesthesia.
